newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish fruit exporter to float partial shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish fruit exporter to float partial shares.

text.p: Turkey's leading fruit and vegetable exporter Unal Tarim Urunleri Ihracat ve Sanayi AS said it would float shares representing 40.8 percent of its capital in a two-day public offer beginning on Thursday.
The fixed price will be 12,000 lira per 1,000 lira nominal valued share in the offer to be lead-managed by Global securities, Unal Tarim said in a press release.
The company will waive 27.699 billion lira ($168,000) of preemptive rights to offer them to the public when raising its capital to 166.195 billion lira from 138.496 billion.
It will also offer 40.166 billion lira of old shares, bringing the total to 67.865 billion lira.
Of the total offer, 33.865 billion lira will be allocated to investors abroad. The consortium managing the offer includes Aks securities and Evgin securities.
Unal Tarim is owned 70 percent by the Unal family and 29 percent by Cosmos Trust series Turkish supreme Fund B and one percent by Sparx Asset Management.

The company which runs Turkey's biggest integrated fruit and vegetable processing plant as well as packaging units and cold storages in western Turkey, said it aimed to raise its turnover to $18 million this year from $13 million in 1996.
Its operating profit was $1.14 million last year.

Unal Tarim which currently exports to 12 countries in Europe, plans to further diversify its line of products by setting up a company in Moscow, a dried fruit plant and a concentrated fruit plant in western Turkey in 1997 and 1998.
